title: Why Can't You Breathe and SWALLOW at the Same Time? 🫁
description:
Swallow... and try to breathe in at the same time. You can't. Air and spit share ONE tunnel at the back of your throat, so on every swallow your brain hits pause on breathing for about a second, your voice box hops up (feel your throat jump), and a little lid, the epiglottis, folds down over your windpipe while your spit slides past into the food pipe. When the lid is a little late, a sip goes down the wrong pipe and you cough it back out. You do this hundreds of times a day: one study counted about 600 swallows a day. Could you?
